HotLoop Flow 2.16.0 lets one flow file, and so one set of FlowLab diagrams, be pushed to every Flow install a tenant runs in EmberNet, with a check after each one, and a failed one put back. It also lets two installs share one job, with a lease that makes sure only one of them writes to equipment at a time. It is amd64 first, with arm64 following in 2.16.1.

## What's new

- **Push to a tenant's stations (#201).** `hotloop-flow stations list -tenant ID` and `hotloop-flow stations push -tenant ID -file flows.json` put one flow file on each Flow install EmberNet shows as running for the tenant, one at a time. The stations come from the EmberNet dashboard and are never typed in, and a row of any other tenant is dropped. After each deploy the station must answer the revision every station is to have, have no node that failed to start, and have every diagram of the file that starts by itself present and running or finished. A station that fails is rolled back to the deployment it was on and the push stops; the report says which stations were done, failed, skipped and never started. A push that would restart a running logger changes nothing until the operator says yes at the prompt, passes `-confirm-restart`, or gives a `-window` that holds now. `docs/stations.md` is the page.
- **The same push over the API and MCP (#201).** `GET /stations` and `POST /stations/push`, and the MCP tools `list_stations` and `push_to_stations`, which brings the tools to 43. They are there only where the four stations settings are set.
- **A warm standby with a fencing lease (#204).** Two Flow installs can share one job. One PostgreSQL row holds a lease and a number that rises each time the holder changes. The holder checks the lease right before every write to equipment, in the Modbus, S7, OPC UA and EtherNet/IP write nodes, the HotLoop script and recipe nodes, and the FlowLab diagram writes to HotLoop, instruments and serial ports. A standby, or a holder that has lost its lease, has its write refused with a counted error before anything is sent, and the standby takes the lease over after the active one's lease runs out. `GET /failover` and the MCP tool `get_failover`, which brings the tools to 44, say whether this install is active, standby or lost, who holds the lease and how many writes were held back. The editor shows a banner on a standby, in the 13 languages, and `docs/failover.md` is the page.
- **Chart values and Quadlet lines for it (#204).** `failover.urlSecret`, `failover.name`, `failover.ttl`, `failover.renewEvery` and `failover.writeMargin` in the chart, with the Secret holding the PostgreSQL URL mounted as a file, and the environment variables and Podman secret for a Quadlet unit in `docs/deploying.md`.
- **Chart values and Quadlet lines (#202).** `stations.dashboardUrl`, `stations.tenant`, `stations.dashboardTokenSecret` and `stations.deployTokenSecret` in the chart, with the two Secrets mounted as files, and the four environment variables and two mounted secrets for a Quadlet unit in `docs/deploying.md`.

## What changed

- A start whose failover settings could let the active run short of lease between renewals, such as a write margin as long as the lease, is refused.
- A start with only some of the four stations settings is refused, and so is a chart render with some of them. All four or none.
- A token that pushes to stations needs `status.read` as well as `flows.read` and `flows.write`, because the check after each deploy reads the station's diagrams. `hotloop-flow token` now prints that, and so do the README and the stations page. A plain deploy token still works for `deploy` as before.
- The revision a flow set will have once saved can now be known before it is saved, from one function the save also uses. Nothing about revisions changed.
- The docs name `hotloop-flow-mcp-server` where they said `mcp-server` (#197, #199, #200).
- The static binary is 51,859,618 bytes (49 MiB), under the 50 MiB budget in `ci.yml`.

## New settings

`stations.dashboardUrl`, `stations.tenant`, `stations.dashboardTokenFile` and `stations.deployTokenFile` in the config file, or `HOTLOOP_FLOW_STATIONS_DASHBOARD_URL`, `HOTLOOP_FLOW_STATIONS_TENANT`, `HOTLOOP_FLOW_STATIONS_DASHBOARD_TOKEN_FILE` and `HOTLOOP_FLOW_STATIONS_DEPLOY_TOKEN_FILE`. All empty by default, which leaves the feature off. In the chart they are the `stations.*` values above.

`failover.urlFile`, `failover.name`, `failover.holder`, `failover.ttl`, `failover.renewEvery` and `failover.writeMargin` in the config file, or `HOTLOOP_FLOW_FAILOVER_URL_FILE`, `HOTLOOP_FLOW_FAILOVER_NAME`, `HOTLOOP_FLOW_FAILOVER_HOLDER`, `HOTLOOP_FLOW_FAILOVER_TTL`, `HOTLOOP_FLOW_FAILOVER_RENEW_EVERY` and `HOTLOOP_FLOW_FAILOVER_WRITE_MARGIN`. The name defaults to `flow`, the holder to the host name, the ttl to 15 seconds, the renewal to a third of it and the write margin to 5 seconds. With no URL file the feature is off and every write goes out as before. In the chart they are the `failover.*` values above.

## Upgrade

A plain `helm upgrade` to the 2.16.0 image and chart, or the new tag in your Quadlet unit. Nothing happens on first start and nothing needs migrating. A flow file loads and saves byte for byte as before. This release is amd64 only: arm64 boxes stay on 2.15.1 until 2.16.1, which is the same code with the arm64 image added.

Image: `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop-flow:2.16.0`, linux/amd64 first, with arm64 following in 2.16.1. Chart: `https://hotloop.io/hotloop-flow/`. The README at this tag has the rest, with pictures: https://github.com/HotLoop-io/hotloop-flow/blob/v2.16.0/README.md
